newsitem.title: CHINA: China firms blame losses on overstaffing.
newsitem.headline: China firms blame losses on overstaffing.

text.p: Most of China's state-owned firms blame their recurrent losses on overstaffing and capital shortages, said a survey issued by the China Business Daily on Monday.
About 92.3 percent of enterprises believe the burden of huge numbers of surplus workers employed in state firms was among the three main reasons behind their losses, the survey said.
About 76.3 percent of state firms listed capital shortages as one of the three reasons why some had stopped production and 60 percent cited the burden of social welfare costs, it said.
The survey by the State Statistical Bureau questioned 435 state firms in 29 provinces and cities, the newspaper said.

About 75 percent of China's more than 100,000 state firms lost money last year and total losses in the government sector soared to 69 billion yuan ($8.3 billion) between January and October, a year-on-year rise of 45 percent, state media has said.
Loss-making enterprises were concentrated in eight sectors, including textiles, transport, food processing and the chemical industry, the newspaper said.

Most of the inefficient state enterprises were in the northeastern provinces, with 265 in Liaoning, 208 in southwestern Sichuan province and 162 in southern Guangdong province, it said but gave no further details.
